findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following facility items in need of repair:
1. The shelving in the walk-in cooler was observed rusted and in need of repair. Inspector recommends sealing the shelving with paint or replacing with coated shelving to prevent future rust accumulation.

2. The walk-in freezer has an accumulation of ice on food containers, walls, ceiling, floors, and shelving. Inspector recommends defrosting and cleaning the freezer. If accumulation persists, the freezer will require repair. 

Ensure these physical facility items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food items in the salad bar to be out of the appropriate temperature range : 
1. Sliced tomato (54F)
2. Cooked chicken (52F)
3. Sliced cucumber (51F)
4. Cut lettuce (41F)
5. Shredded cheese (high-moisture, 49F)
6. Ranch, 7 bottles (49-52F)
7. Italian dressing (52F)
8. French dressing (53F)
9. Fat-free ranch (52F)

All of these temperatures were measured with a probe thermometer. The cut tomato, shredded cheese, chicken, and salad dressings (original package labeled “refrigerate after opening”) were voluntarily discarded. The cut lettuce, since the temperature was at the safety threshold, was placed back into the walk-in cooler to ensure safe cold holding until lunch. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain in the salad bar cooler.  The food had been in the salad bar cooler since 9am, and failed to reach a safe temperature. Lunch is served from 11am-1:30pm, so time as a control will be utilized for the new salad bar items. These items will be discarded again after lunch. PIC was informed that TCS foods can only be kept out of temp for a maximum of 4 hours and must be discarded after use. PIC was reminded that a time log must be maintained to record what time foods must be discarded after being placed on the salad bar.  PIC will be using time as a control until the salad bar cooler is repaired and can maintain foods at a temperature of 41F or below. For more information regarding the salad bar cooler, see violation #33.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed that the salad bar is failing to maintain food temperatures at 41F or below. The PIC is aware of the issue and will be submitting a work order to fix the salad bar. Until then, PIC will use time as a control for all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods on the salad bar. See violation #22 for more information regarding the impacted food in the salad bar cooler. A follow-up is scheduled for 10 days (3/6/2025) to check cold holding temperatures in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
Observed sanitizer buckets to be at zero ppm of Quat sanitizer. The buckets were remade. Dish machine and 3 part sink are registering with compliant sanitizer concentrations.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed the hot holding unit to have food holding at 110F. The independent internal thermometer is reading 100F. The food went into hot holding cabinet at around 11:50am according to chef. 3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed that the hot holding cabinet appears to be broken and rigged with non food materials (tape) in order to keep the unit functioning properly Repair or replace the cabinet so that it is holding food at the proper temperature. Do not use cabinet for hot holding until the unit is repaired or replaced  4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0-10 ppm at three compartment sink. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114. The facility has sanitizer to add to the sink manually. Do not use the automatic dispenser until it can be repaired. The provider was out recently according to the manager on duty and the dispenser was working. It is the responsibility of the facility to check the dispenser at the start of every day, before use.  Check other sanitizing equipment also before use and periodically through the day.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine measured at 0 ppm chlorine concentration. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114. The machine water was dumped, the machine primed and it began to function properly.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14  (P) Sausage gravy is observed to be 109F in the middle when tested with a probe thermometer. Food did not cool from 135?F to 70F within two hours. The food was placed into the cooler at 9am and temperature was taken after 11:15am. The food was immediately discarded. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.14.
